title: Five ways to make your colour last longer
excerpt: Cooler water, fewer washes and a gloss between visits. Small habits that keep colour bright for weeks longer.
content:
Colour fades for the same few reasons. Here's what we tell every client.

Wash less, and cooler

Hot water opens the hair and lets colour out. Lukewarm is kinder.

Use a colour-safe shampoo

Sulphate-free shampoos are gentler on colour.

Book a gloss

A quick gloss between colours brings back the shine and tone.

title: Caring for curls: what we tell every curly client
excerpt: Less brushing, more water and the right cut. Ollie and Jess on getting the most from curly hair.
content:
Curly hair needs a different routine. These are the basics.

Don't brush it dry

Brush or comb curls only when they're wet and full of conditioner.

Get a dry cut

Cutting curls dry, one by one, shows the shape as you'll wear it.

Air dry or diffuse

Scrunch in a cream or gel and leave it alone while it dries.

title: Wedding hair: a timeline from trial to the big day
excerpt: When to book, when to trial and what to do the night before. Jess's guide for brides and bridesmaids.
content:
Jess has done the hair for more than forty weddings. Here's how she plans them.

Six months before

Book the date. Saturdays in summer go first.

Two months before

Have a trial, with your veil or accessories if you have them.

The night before

Wash your hair. Day-old hair holds pins and curls best.

title: Growing your brows back after years of plucking
excerpt: It takes patience, a good map and a little help from tint. Bea on getting full brows back.
content:
Most of Bea's new clients have over-plucked at some point. Here's how she helps.

Stop plucking

Leave them alone for eight weeks, even the strays.

Map them

Bea maps the shape that suits your face, so you know which hairs to keep.

Tint helps

A tint makes fine, new hairs show up while they grow.
